2017 and of course big blue congratulations giving a commencement
speech is a daunting task I thought when I finished grad school I was done with homework but I got to do some homework to prepare for today and when I started I have to say I found more
questions than answers like why doesn't anyone deliver Aggie ice cream to Philly is stealing the Wagon Wheel an accomplishment I could list on my

resume I didn't find any answers to these questions and I decided it was time to get down to business as a psychologist I did what any self-respecting social scientist would do I started reading studies of
graduation speeches to find out what are these all about and I decided that I would give a graduation speech about graduation speeches I was hoping it would be like
that Seinfeld episode with the coffee table book about coffee tables but that's the wrong generation it'll be like when Ryan Gosling wore a shirt with a picture of mccauly culin on
it and then Molly culin wore a shirt with a picture of Ryan Gosling wearing that shirt so today I want to give a metag graduation speech I want to tell you
what I think is missing from other graduation speeches it turns out that almost every commencement speech is about virtues you all know virtues well here living by a
set of worthy principles and it turns out it's pretty easy to be virtuous when things are going well in your life it's when you're down that your virtues really get
tested last week Facebook coo and I Cheryl sanberg published a book option about building resilience we all face challenges in life whether it's a failed
exam or a failed marriage the loss of a football game or the loss of a loved one and resilience is the muscle that gets us through these events in the face of
adversity how do we find the strength to stand by our values to stick to our virtues well when you look at graduation speeches there are three virtues that
turn out to be really popular they generosity authenticity and grit and if you want to live by these virtues you will need resilience in your life you need resilience to stay
generous on the days when you lose faith in humanity you need resilience to stay true to yourself on the days when other people have lost faith in you and you
need resilience to persevere on the days when you've lost faith in yourself I love these virtues but I do worry that if you're too obsessed with any of them you might under mind your
own resilience and the reason for that is that virtues are a little bit like vitamins are critical for your health but what happens if you take more
vitamins than your body needs I hope none of you have run the personal experiment to find out but it turns out that some vitamins like vitamin C nothing bad will happen
no harm done if you take too much vitamin C but other vitamins like vitamin D are dangerous in large doses they can cause serious kidney problems there was a great philosopher named
Aristotle who believed that virtues were a lot like vitamin D he thought that too little of a virtue was bad but so was too much and he argued that every virtue
sits in the middle between the vices of deficiency and the vices of excess too little humor is dry too much is silly too little pride makes us Meek too much
makes us narcissists too much self-restraint leaves you doing homework while your friends are tailgating and too little self-restraint means you are really going to regret eating that
fourth Scotsman dog well if you're not a fan of the ancient Greeks the same point was made by another great philosopher named
Goldilocks teaches us that like porridge virtues can run too hot or too cold more is not always better my colleague Barry Schwarz and I have
argued that if you want happiness and success you need to find The Sweet Spot between the extremes of too little and too much you need to look for that just right so let's talk about how this plays
out for the major virtues that show up in commencement speeches generosity it's the single most common theme in graduation speeches help others that's
the message of nearly two-thirds of them and I'm a huge fan of generosity I've spent my whole career studying it I wrote an entire book about how it can not only drive our happiness but also
our success I found in the long run givers tend to outperform takers and if you don't believe that look no further than these amazing benefactors here John and Karen Huntsman they are living proof
of the power of generosity and it's true across so many different professions it's true for engineers salespeople doctors and even if giving does not guarantee more success than taking it
just turns out to be a more meaningful way to live our lives but there's such a thing as being too generous if you are too generous that turns out to be a recipe for
Burnout take teachers education is all about helping students so we tend to love teachers who are selfless but in some research I did with a colleague Reb we actually found that the most

selfless teachers ended up being the least engaged in the classroom and their students did the worst on standardized achievement tests so you know what this means about the best teachers they had about as much
compassion as Frank Underwood if you were about maybe half a Gorgan no the effective teachers were the ones who cared really deeply about their students but they also did what
were all advised to do on airplanes they secured their own oxygen Mass before assisting others now if you're George Carlin you laughed at that advice saying I do not
need to be told that but this is critical advice for living a good life the teachers who said I am going to care
about students but not at my own expense they felt less altruistic but they actually helped more they were able to give in ways that were energizing instead of exhausting and ways that
ultimately were sustainable so my advice today is help others but don't sacrifice yourselves a second beloved virt is
authenticity be true to yourself it's a Core theme in more than half of commencement speeches and I'm not going to encourage anyone in this room to be false to yourself of course you should
be genuine but if authenticity is the virtue you prize most in life there is a real danger that you will stunt your own growth to be authentic you have to be
crystal clear about your identity and values who am I what's important to me you need to know the answers to those questions and if you get clear about the answer to those questions that can
tether you to a fixed anchor and close the door to personal growth when I was in grad school a friend asked me to give a guest lecture for her class I was terrified of public speaking but I
wanted to be helpful so I agreed and I thought as a learning opportunity after the class I'll give out feedback forms to find out how I can get better and let
me just tell you it was brutal one student wrote that I was so nervous that I was causing all the students to physically shake in their
seats I was shaking too and let's face it my authentic self was not a fan of public speaking but you know what I've started volunteering to give more guest lectures anyway knowing it was the only
way that I could improve and I was not being true to myself I was being true to the self that I wanted to become someone who was comfortable on stage giving speeches well a few years later I was
turned down for my first Professor job because after watching me give a presentation the hiring committee said I would never ever be able to teach a group of students great message for a
new professor right and I ended up getting hired by a different School my first year there I was asked to teach a 4-Hour class for Colonels in the US Air
Force I was 25 they were twice my age they had dozens of medals on their uniforms thousands of flight hours under their belts and billions of dollars in
budgets under their command plus they all had cool nicknames like Striker and sandune it was like a scene out of the movie Top Gun and I knew I needed to
establish credibility so I started sharing my credentials and at the end of the session their feedback forms were even less fun than the ones from college
students one of the Air Force Colonels wrote there was more quality information in the audience than on the podium dagger to the

experience was that never give up is actually really bad advice sometimes quitting is a virtue and if you want to cultivate the virtue of grit that doesn't mean keep doing the thing that's
failing over and over again it means defining your dreams broadly enough that you can find new ways to pursue them when your first and second plans fail I needed to give up on my dream of making

your failures when I got tenure and decided to write my first book my literary agent asked for a proposal and I did something I would never wish on my worst enemy which is I got so excited
about the ideas that I ended up accidentally writing the whole book instead of just the proposal over 102,000 words I sent it over and my agent gently told me that my writing
might interest a fellow academic but that was about it and no person in their right mind would ever read a sentence that I wrote so if I believed in this idea of never give up I might have gone to
another agent or I might have gone to Publishers directly but resilience meant having the strength to take the feedback to heart and start over I had the same goal writing a book about generosity but
a different strategy writing something that people might actually want to read should have thought of that before the 102,000 words and my agent gave me brilliant advice he said write like you
teach so I started over from scratch and I threw out over a 100,000 words there were a few hundred that I couldn't let go of which I sort of snuck into the book but the book that I wrote that time
